title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An Avride self-driving vehicle in Austin struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood, with a human safety operator present in the car. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after hitting the duck. The failure was in object detection and response, where the system either did not recognize the duck as an obstacle or did not treat it as one requiring evasive action.

The incident reveals a gap between what a deployed autonomous system was built to handle and what it encountered. A duck in a roadway is a real-world obstacle that a production vehicle in neighborhoods must account for. Catching this failure would have required the system to detect and respond appropriately to small animals in its path before deployment in mixed-use areas, or human review of how the vehicle responds to such objects when a safety operator is present.

It is not established whether the system lacked the ability to detect the duck, failed to classify it as an obstacle, or was operating within its design specifications but in conditions beyond its actual capability.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, was well-known to residents, intensifying their concern about autonomous vehicle safety in their area.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and investigated the situation by reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene in simulation. The company denies a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it came to complete stops at all relevant signs. In response, Avride has restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now running controlled experiments to improve the technology's ability to avoid similar situations without compromising overall safety performance.
